title: Potunk Neck (Westhampton)
summary: Potunk is a Westhampton placename for Potunk Neck and nearby meadowland, recorded in seventeenth-century Southampton and East Hampton references and interpreted as a boggy place.
map_geometry_source: Approximate Westhampton point for Potunk Neck, placed between nearby Apocock/Beaverdam Creek, Monabaugs, and Ketchaponack records; exact neck, point, and meadow boundaries need local map review.
introduction_content: Potunk is a Native name for a Westhampton neck and meadow landscape. Its appearance in the 1659 Ogden deed and later meadow divisions connects it with the wider history of colonial claims to Shinnecock land. Tooker, pp. 196–197
history_content:
The May 12, 1659 deed used Potuncke as a boundary reference. Later records divided meadows and uplands among colonial proprietors; the 1686 description placed Potunk beside Monabaugs swamp. Those transactions preserved Native names while changing the terms under which land was claimed and allocated. Tooker, pp. 196–197

The 1686 town-book descriptions can be read together to compare the neighboring necks, waterways and crossings. Southampton town records, vol. II, printed pp. 113–114
translation_content:
Related forms include Potuncke, Potunck, Potunk, and Potonke. The name is interpreted as a bog, a place where the foot sinks, or land where one sinks in mire.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are among the most interesting and powerful documents we have for exploring changes to landscape over time.”

— William Cronon, Names on the Land: Place Names as Historical Evidence (2018), Section I, Why study place names?
whereintheworld_content: The point indicates the general Potunk vicinity in Westhampton. The older neck cannot be reduced to the modern Potunk Point label: the sources also describe meadows, upland and Monabaugs swamp. The pin is approximate, and the historical bounds are not precise enough for a land polygon. Tooker, pp. 196–197
